basis: P5CS-deficiency spastic paraplegia; persistent pes cavus is frequent (30-79%). Cataracts, hearing impairment and urinary manifestations are below 30%.

decisions.musculoskeletal: involved: persistent pes cavus is a structural skeletal deformity reported in 30-79%; weakness alone would not qualify.

basis: Developmental impairment and congenital heart anomalies are defining common features in the definition. Scoliosis and pigmentation abnormalities are occasional (5-29%).

decisions.cardiovascular: primary: congenital heart anomalies are explicitly among the syndrome's most common defining features; their inclusion does not depend on an inferred numerical frequency.

basis: Biofilm-mediated acid demineralization destroys dental hard tissue in pits and fissures. Teeth belong to the gastrointestinal axis.

decisions.infectious_immune: none: caries is a sugar-driven, biofilm-mediated dysbiotic disease; bacterial participation alone does not establish an infectious or immune-mediated diagnosis.

basis: P5CS metabolic deficiency causes spastic neurodevelopmental disease. Muscle atrophy (4/6) and incontinence (4/6) reflect neural dysfunction; cataract occurs in only 1/6.

decisions.musculoskeletal: none: muscle wasting in 4/6 reflects denervation from the neurologic disease, without evidence of direct myopathy; kyphoscoliosis is occasional (5-29%).

basis: Storage disease with defining dysostosis (26/29); intellectual disability and corneal opacity each 80-99%. Airway/pleural involvement omitted at cap; hepatomegaly alone lacks dysfunction.

decisions.musculoskeletal: primary: skeletal dysplasia is a defining component, supported by the skeletal-involvement parent, dysostosis in 26/29 and joint restriction in 22/26.

basis: Brain malformations/developmental impairment and coloboma/ptosis define the syndrome. Sensorineural hearing impairment occurs in roughly 30-40%; cardiac defects are less common.

decisions.otologic: involved: sensorineural hearing impairment affects approximately 30-40% over the usual course and represents lasting auditory dysfunction.

basis: SFTPC dysfunction causes intrinsic alveolar/interstitial lung disease. Pulmonary hypertension and developmental delay each occur in 2/17; recurrent pneumonia is separately diagnosed.

decisions.metabolic_endocrine: none: SFTPC-related disease is an intrinsic pneumocyte/surfactant disorder; the name's use of metabolism does not establish an endocrine or systemic metabolic disease.

basis: Developmental impairment/neuropathy; heart and renal malformations each 30-79%, strabismus 6/15 (40%). Skeletal findings omitted at cap; constipation alone lacks direct injury.

decisions.ocular: involved: persistent strabismus occurs in 6/15 (40%), establishing common ocular dysfunction.
decisions.musculoskeletal: none: atrophy is neurogenic; frequent foot abnormalities/hypermobility are lower priority than the retained organ abnormalities under the four-axis cap.

basis: Congenital thymic aplasia causes defining quantitative and functional T-cell deficiency. Pneumonias and gastrointestinal infections are separate secondary diseases.

decisions.haematologic: primary: defining T-lymphocyte deficiency includes reduced blood-cell numbers, satisfying the explicit blood-cell disease rule alongside the immune mechanism.

basis: Glycosylation disorder with intrinsic immunodeficiency and coagulopathy (80-99%); developmental delay in 2/2 and CNS/PNS abnormalities in 30-79%. Three required mechanism axes occupy primary.

decisions.haematologic: primary: decreased coagulation factors define the disease, with coagulation abnormalities in 80-99%; the coagulation mechanism requires this primary axis.
decisions.neurologic: involved: developmental delay in 2/2 and CNS/PNS abnormalities in 30-79%; the three primary slots are occupied by required metabolic, immune and blood/coagulation axes.
